runs.name: Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, Inc.; NYSE WH; the world's largest hotel franchisor by number of franchised properties, over 8,300 hotels under 25 brands; spun off from Wyndham Worldwide, now Travel + Leisure, in 2018; La Quinta bought 2018; no rival named in the 10-K, Choice, Hilton and Marriott chosen by the analyst
runs.entry: Price **$73.42** (close 2026-10-13; aggregator quote printed by `tools/run.py`, flagged). Shares **74,211,122**, one class (10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30, filed 2026-07-23, accession 0001722684-26-000074, cover as of 2026-07-15; `cover_shares.py`; checked against 76.1M issued less 1.6M treasury = 74.5M at 2026-06-30, the difference the buyback since; after the 10-Q only Forms 3, 4 and 144 filed); cap **$5,449M**. Sovereign **5.56%** (US Treasury daily par yield curve, 30-year, 2026-10-13). Filings read: 10-K FY2025 (0001722684-26-000007), 10-Q Q2 2026, DEF 14A filed 2026-03-25 (0001722684-26-000050), six 8-Ks 2025-11-04 to 2026-05-18, 10-Ks FY2019, FY2021 and FY2023 for the cycle; one figure cross-checked (FY2025 operating cash $367M on the filed statement against the tool's 367.0, FY2023 and FY2024 likewise). Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7 (the brief's departure), stated in the run file; the 10-K names no rival company (confirmed by search), so Choice, Hilton and Marriott were chosen as a CONVENTION of the run and read from their own 10-Ks for 2019 and 2025; IHG and Hyatt not read. **Q1 IN**: a franchisor whose economics are rooms, RevPAR, the royalty rate and what it pays owners to sign, all filed every year. **Q2 IN, narrowly**: pre-tax returns on tangible capital 36% to 67%, but U.S. rooms 510,200 (2019) to 505,100 (2025) and U.S. properties 6,342 to 5,934; royalties and franchise fees +12.7% over six years ($480M to $541M) against about +65% at Hilton and Marriott; development advances $19M to $112M a year, 21% of core fees; 56% of rooms signed 2021 to 2025 only replaced rooms that left; system rooms +11% at Choice (with Radisson), +39% at Hilton, +29% at Marriott; return on tangible capital falling since 2022. **Q3 WEIGHS AGAINST**: little capital needed, but the +$272M added since 2022 earned about 14% pre-tax against 63% on the 2022 base. **Q4 no STOP, WEIGHS AGAINST**: ten balance sheets read, no confusion or suspicion; featured adjusted EBITDA and an 'adjusted free cash flow' ($433M) that excludes development advances, guidance every year; goodwill and brands 72% of assets (La Quinta), equity $1,418M to $468M through $1.9B of buybacks, debt to $2,675M, other non-current assets $226M to $685M explained by disclosed advances to owners. **Q5 integrity IN** (no doubt about honesty found; presentational habits against); ability weighs against (weakest of four franchisors on unit and fee growth; the $160M Revo loss, Revo about 22,000 rooms failing January 2026; CFO departure November 2025, Chief Accounting Officer departure 2026-07-31; the CEO's illness disclosed openly, not weighed). **Q6 Part A WEIGHS AGAINST** (paid out $2,546M 2019 to 2025, dividends $730M and buybacks $1,816M, against about $1,461M of owner cash, partly borrowed; buybacks with no stated price at $69 to $86, above the top of the range), **Part B WEIGHS AGAINST**. Owner cash (operating cash less stock pay, capital expenditure, finance-lease principal and net loans to owners; development advances inside operating cash; the 2019 La Quinta tax payment of $195M treated as an acquisition; a one-time $76M card-partner advance removed from 2025; interest added back after the filer's 25% outlook rate) **$289.1M** a year all-equity all spending and **$320.6M** maintenance-only, before interest, on the cycle 2019 to 2025 (2021 aberrational on the filer's own description as a recovery year; literal window 2021 to 2025 beside); not a serial acquirer; the split of development advances into maintenance and growth by the replacement share a CONVENTION of the run. **Q7 OUT**: value **$34.94 to $42.59** a share (all-equity, central, no growth, one cycle having no successor) at 5.56% less net debt $2,606M, against **$73.42**; no case earns the floor (best 3.98% central, 4.70% on the literal window, about 6.5% in a generous 1.8% growth case worth $70.76 beside), none earns even the Treasury; equity-only $50.58 to $58.23, literal window top $52.87 and bottom -$8.94 beside. Fair **$5.96** all-equity (central), **$30.25** equity-only. Facts after the stop, not weighed: debt $2,675M at 2026-06-30 (term loan B $1.5B due 2030 about 95% swapped to fixed, the swaps expiring Q4 2027 to Q3 2028; $500M 4.375% notes 2028; $650M 5.625% notes 2033; $27M revolver; $15M Revo hotel mortgages), Ba1 / BB+, first-lien leverage 2.8x against a 5.0x covenant, interest coverage 2.9x in 2025; franchisee credit (advances $343M, loans $88M gross) and a construction-loan guarantee programme; Q12: human-trafficking litigation at franchised hotels named in Item 1A, exposure beyond accruals for all legal matters up to about $7M. Contamination declared by the analyst: a date-filtered listing of `Test Runs/` showing the CHH, HLT, MAR and four steel run names dated 2026-10-14, and the CHH fold commit subject in its session context naming a Wyndham ratio; neither opened or used, the rival figures computed from the rivals' own filings. Commits 9e793a2e, f6f113c9, cba0b21c, 122a12fb, 0430df31, 47dc63c7, 14d66e14, 5c069f32, 1019c71b (write-early kept, a commit per question). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's check clean (81 ids); the dispatcher's `_dispatcher_cite_check.py` 81 ids, 20 quoted cites, no missing id, no E-id, no slip. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) specific (a) when a year is low in earnings but high in cash (2021 here: the reading moved the top from $52.87 to $42.59, not the box); (2) key money inside operating cash is neither capital expenditure nor working capital in the text, so the maintenance split was confessed; (3) specific (c) and a sale of owned hotels that is not a business sale ($9.11 a share beside); (4) how a negative end case enters the fair-price average; (5) Q2 is binary where the evidence is a slope, a standing castle narrowing; (6) the equity-only figure exceeds the all-equity range whenever debt costs less after tax than the long Treasury, and the reason may need stating beside the two reporting figures. Could not get: the 2025 annual-report letter (PDF only), IHG and Hyatt, Hilton's and Marriott's 2019 U.S. room counts, any split of advances between new and replacement rooms.
runs.narr: OUT at Q7 after Q1 IN, Q2 IN narrowly (a franchisor with pre-tax returns on tangible capital of 36% to 67%, but U.S. rooms 510,200 to 505,100 and properties 6,342 to 5,934 over 2019 to 2025, core fees +12.7% in six years against about +65% at Hilton and Marriott, development advances $19M to $112M a year, 56% of rooms signed 2021 to 2025 only replacing rooms that left), Q3 against (the capital added since 2022 earned about 14% pre-tax), Q4 no STOP with adjusted EBITDA and an 'adjusted free cash flow' excluding the advances against, Q5 integrity IN with ability against (the $160M Revo loss, finance turnover), Q6 against on both parts ($2,546M paid out against about $1,461M of owner cash, partly borrowed, buybacks at $69 to $86 with no stated price). Owner cash $289.1M all spending, $320.6M maintenance-only, cycle 2019 to 2025 with 2021 aberrational; net debt $2,606M. Value $34.94 to $42.59 against $73.42 at the 5.56% Treasury, no case earning the floor or the Treasury; fair $5.96 all-equity, $30.25 equity-only, armed. Framework gaps for the operator: a year low in earnings and high in cash under specific (a); key money inside operating cash; an owned-hotel sale under specific (c); a negative end case in the fair price; a narrowing castle under a binary Q2; why equity-only exceeds all-equity.
runs.fair_label: WH v5 fair price, all-equity: $5.96 a share (equity-only $30.25). Run 2026-10-14 (Test Runs/2026-10-14 Run - WH Wyndham Hotels & Resorts.md; OUT at Q7 at $73.42; value range $34.94 to $42.59 at the 5.56% Treasury). Reporting figure, a prompt to re-run Q7, not a buy signal.
